pediatric-oncology.title: Paediatric Oncology
pediatric-oncology.lead: Paediatric oncology focuses on the diagnosis, treatment and long-term follow-up of cancers in children and adolescents up to the age of 18, including solid tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias. Childhood cancers behave differently from adult cancers and call for care designed around young patients and their families. MedLuxLife coordinates assessments and treatment at our partner hospital, helping families with records, appointments, travel and communication throughout the course of care.
cards: Diagnosis and staging
Thorough evaluation of suspected childhood tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias to establish the diagnosis and the extent of the disease.
Surgery
Surgical removal of tumours may form part of the treatment plan, depending on tumour type and spread.
Chemotherapy
Drug-based cancer treatment planned individually for each child, delivered on an inpatient or outpatient basis.
Radiotherapy
Radiation treatment may be recommended for certain tumour types as part of a combined plan.
Immunotherapy
Treatments that engage the immune system can be considered for selected childhood cancers.
Stem cell transplantation
Stem cell transplantation is among the treatment options for some childhood cancers and blood diseases.
Paediatric haematology-oncology clinic
Outpatient and inpatient care in a dedicated paediatric haematology-oncology clinic, with single rooms that allow a parent to stay with the child during monitoring and treatment.
Outpatient chemotherapy unit
A day unit for short treatments and blood transfusions, so that many children can return home the same day.
Dedicated children's outpatient floor
Outpatient consultations take place on a separate floor reserved for children with cancer, leukaemia and blood diseases.
Long-term follow-up
Structured follow-up after treatment to monitor recovery and the child's ongoing health.
list: Wilms' tumour and other kidney tumours
Soft tissue sarcomas (muscle and connective tissue tumours)
docs_extra: Pathology and biopsy reports
Previous imaging (MRI, CT or PET-CT) on CD/DVD with reports

pediatric-rheumatology.title: Paediatric Rheumatology
pediatric-rheumatology.lead: Paediatric rheumatology covers the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of inflammatory and rheumatic conditions in childhood, which can affect the joints, muscles, blood vessels and skin as well as other organ systems. Because these conditions often differ from their adult forms, care is planned with a multidisciplinary approach. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and follow-up at our partner hospital and supports families throughout their stay.
cards: Specialist assessment
Careful evaluation of joint, muscle, skin and systemic symptoms in children to reach a clear diagnosis.
Recurrent fever evaluation
Investigation of unexplained or recurring fevers, including possible autoinflammatory causes.
Inflammatory joint disease
Diagnosis and treatment planning for juvenile arthritis and related joint conditions.
Vasculitis and multisystem disease
Care for conditions that inflame blood vessels or affect several organs at once.
Multidisciplinary care
Collaboration with other paediatric specialties when a condition involves more than the musculoskeletal system.
Long-term follow-up
Ongoing monitoring to help control disease activity and support the child's quality of life.
docs_extra: Previous blood test results, including inflammatory markers

pediatric-surgery.title: Paediatric Surgery
pediatric-surgery.lead: Paediatric surgery deals with conditions requiring surgical care in infants, children and adolescents, from the prenatal period up to the age of 18. Treatment is tailored to the child's age and development, with open, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques available. MedLuxLife coordinates consultations, surgery dates and aftercare at our partner hospital, so that families can focus on their child.
cards: Prenatal consultation
Surgical evaluation can begin before birth when a condition requiring surgery is identified during pregnancy.
Digestive system surgery
Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of surgical conditions affecting the digestive tract in children.
Urinary tract surgery
Surgical care for conditions of the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract in childhood.
Chest surgery (non-cardiac)
Treatment of surgical conditions within the chest cavity, excluding the heart.
Open, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques
Alongside conventional surgery, endoscopic and laparoscopic methods are used where suitable.
Day surgery
Many procedures allow same-day discharge, including inguinal hernia repair, hydrocele repair, treatment of undescended testicles, circumcision, catheter placement and endoscopic procedures.
Pain management
Specific pain-relief measures aim to keep children comfortable in hospital and after returning home.
Paediatric urology
In collaboration with the Urology department, surgical and endoscopic treatment of congenital anomalies and acquired problems such as stones and trauma.
Coordinated care
Work with other specialties for conditions such as congenital spinal cord defects and nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting).
list: Vesicoureteral reflux (urine flowing back from the bladder to the kidneys)
docs_extra: Previous ultrasound or imaging reports
Prenatal scan reports, if the condition was identified before birth

pediatrics.title: Paediatrics
pediatrics.lead: The paediatrics department provides diagnosis and treatment for children from birth to 18 years of age, with outpatient clinics, an inpatient ward and intensive care areas designed for children. It is organised into a newborn section (0-28 days) and a child section (0-18 years), with subspecialties working together as a multidisciplinary team. MedLuxLife helps families access the right paediatric specialist at our partner hospital and coordinates appointments, travel and communication.
cards: General paediatric care
Outpatient, inpatient and intensive care services for children aged 0-18 in child-friendly settings.
Newborn care
The neonatal section serves babies up to 28 days old through a neonatal unit, a neonatal observation unit and a neonatal intensive care unit.
Breastfeeding support
The hospital follows the UNICEF and WHO Baby-Friendly approach, with specially trained staff helping mothers establish and maintain breastfeeding.
Paediatric allergy

Testing and treatment for allergic diseases, including skin tests, blood allergy tests, lung function tests, allergen provocation tests, food tests, anaesthetic drug tests and allergy vaccination (immunotherapy).
Paediatric endocrinology
Assessment of hormonal and metabolic problems such as growth disorders, diabetes, thyroid and puberty-related conditions.
Paediatric haematology-oncology
Diagnosis and treatment of blood diseases and childhood cancers, with outpatient and inpatient care in a paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic.
Paediatric gastroenterology, hepatology and nutrition
Care for diseases of the oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, small and large intestine, liver and gallbladder, as well as nutritional disorders.
Paediatric surgery

Treatment of urological, genital, digestive and respiratory conditions and newborn anomalies, including non-cardiac thoracic, oncological, digestive and endocrine surgery, paediatric gynaecology, trauma surgery, diagnostic and interventional endoscopy, and laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures.
Paediatric nephrology
Diagnosis and treatment of congenital and acquired problems of the kidneys, urinary tract, bladder and urethra.
Paediatric rheumatology
Outpatient care for childhood rheumatic diseases affecting joints, muscles, blood vessels and skin.
list: Drug allergy, including allergy to anaesthetic agents
Diseases of the oesophagus, stomach and intestines
docs_extra: Child's vaccination record
Growth charts or previous paediatric reports

pelvic-pain-and-endometriosis-clinic.title: Pelvic Pain and Endometriosis Clinic
pelvic-pain-and-endometriosis-clinic.lead: Chronic pelvic pain can affect every part of daily life, and finding its cause often requires more than one specialist. This multidisciplinary clinic investigates the nature and origin of pelvic pain, including endometriosis, using diagnostic methods chosen according to each patient's symptoms, and then plans treatment based on current medical evidence. MedLuxLife arranges your evaluation at our partner hospital and supports you with preparation, records and travel.
cards: Detailed pain assessment
A structured consultation explores when, where and how the pain occurs, its intensity and its effect on work and daily life.
Symptom-based diagnostics
Diagnostic methods are selected to match each patient's symptoms in order to identify the cause of the pain.
Endometriosis evaluation
Assessment of endometriosis as a possible cause of pelvic pain, followed by individual treatment planning.
Multidisciplinary team
Women's health specialists work together with urology, gastroenterology, general surgery, physical therapy and psychiatry.
Individual treatment planning
Treatment is planned in line with current developments, with the aim of improving quality of life affected by pain.
Psychological wellbeing
Mood and emotional strain are considered as part of the overall assessment, with psychiatric input available where helpful.
list: When the pain first started and how often it occurs
Where and when the pain appears, and whether it stays in one place
Whether the pain has changed or spread over time
How intense the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10
Whether the pain limits your ability to work
Any link to the menstrual cycle, urination or sexual intercourse
How you would describe the pain (sharp, dull, aching)
The circumstances in which the pain begins
Any connection with eating, sleeping, sex or movement
Possible triggers such as movement, using the toilet, intercourse or medication
Anything that eases or worsens the pain
Any previous treatment for urinary tract or vaginal infections
Recent low mood, depression or feelings of hopelessness
docs_extra: A pain diary covering at least one menstrual cycle
Previous gynaecological ultrasound, MRI or surgical reports

perinatology.title: Perinatology
perinatology.lead: Perinatology, a division of obstetrics and gynaecology, focuses on the health of mother and baby during pregnancy. Alongside routine pregnancy care and delivery, it provides follow-up and management of high-risk pregnancies and the diagnosis and management of maternal and fetal conditions using specialised scans, tests and procedures. MedLuxLife helps expectant parents arrange screening, specialist scans and consultations at our partner hospital and coordinates every step of the visit.
cards: Routine and high-risk pregnancy care
Pregnancy follow-up and delivery, with closer monitoring and management for high-risk pregnancies.
First-trimester screening (11-14 weeks)

An ultrasound nuchal translucency measurement, which can be combined with blood tests and further markers such as the fetal nasal bone, blood flow in the fetal heart and the facial angle, to assess the risk of Down syndrome and other conditions.
Second-trimester screening (15-21 weeks)
A triple or quadruple blood test that estimates risk; a raised result indicates that diagnostic testing may be advisable, not that the baby is affected.
Early detailed anomaly scan (11-14 weeks)
A detailed transvaginal ultrasound examination of fetal development early in pregnancy.
Detailed anomaly scan (18-22 weeks)
A high-resolution second-level ultrasound examining fetal organs and growth, which can include uterine artery Doppler and cervical length assessment in at-risk pregnancies.
Fetal echocardiography

A detailed examination of the baby's heart structure and function, recommended when there is an increased risk of congenital heart disease or a suspected abnormality; ideally performed around 18-21 weeks.
Doppler ultrasound
Maternal and fetal Doppler examinations to assess blood flow to the placenta and within the baby's circulation.
Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)
A placental tissue sample, usually taken at 11-14 weeks under ultrasound guidance, to examine chromosome number and structure.
Amniocentesis
A small sample of amniotic fluid, usually taken at 16-22 weeks, for chromosomal analysis; rapid FISH testing for selected chromosomes may give preliminary results sooner.
Cordocentesis (fetal blood sampling)
A small blood sample from the umbilical cord vein, usually after the 19th week, for diagnostic testing.
Counselling and birth planning
Results are discussed with parents, and findings such as a heart abnormality help plan where and how the birth should take place.
list: 15-21 week screening tests (triple or quadruple test)
11-14 week transvaginal detailed fetal anomaly screening
docs_extra: Maternity record (e.g. Mutterpass) and previous pregnancy scan reports
Previous screening or genetic test results

physical-therapy-and-rehabilitation.title: Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation
physical-therapy-and-rehabilitation.lead: Physical therapy and rehabilitation aims to restore movement and function, reduce pain and improve mobility after injury, illness or surgery. The department offers assessment, treatment and rehabilitation for a wide range of conditions, from musculoskeletal disorders to neurological diseases, along with several specialised programmes. MedLuxLife can arrange a rehabilitation stay at our partner hospital and coordinate it with your other treatment.
cards: Musculoskeletal conditions
Treatment for arthritis, osteoporosis, inflammatory and soft tissue rheumatic diseases, and neck, back and lower back pain.
Orthopaedic rehabilitation
Rehabilitation after fractures and dislocations, sports injuries, spinal curvatures, foot problems and orthopaedic surgery such as joint replacement.
Neurological rehabilitation
Programmes for stroke, brain and spinal cord injury, facial paralysis, nerve injuries, muscle diseases and Parkinson's disease.
Paediatric rehabilitation
Therapy for children with spasticity, aimed at improving movement and daily function.
Cardiac rehabilitation
Supervised exercise and recovery programmes following heart problems.
Pelvic floor and pregnancy programmes
A stress incontinence programme for urinary leakage and guided exercise during pregnancy.
Back school and osteoporosis school
Educational programmes teaching posture, movement and exercise to protect the spine and bones.
Fibromyalgia group programme
Group-based therapy and education for people living with fibromyalgia.
Specialised rehabilitation
Rehabilitation after cosmetic surgery, programmes for dialysis patients, and assessment and planning after obesity surgery.
Treatment for localised sweating
Therapy options for excessive sweating in specific areas of the body.
list: Inflammatory joint diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis
Soft tissue rheumatic diseases such as fibromyalgia and myofascial pain syndrome
Neck, back and lower back pain
Joint stiffness and circulatory problems after fractures or dislocations
Meniscus and ligament injuries and other sports injuries
Flat feet and other foot problems
Rehabilitation before and after orthopaedic surgery, including joint replacement
Assessment and planning after obesity surgery
docs_extra: Surgical or discharge reports from recent operations
Recent X-ray or MRI reports

pituitary-clinic.title: Pituitary Clinic
pituitary-clinic.lead: Pituitary disorders can be difficult to recognise because their symptoms often resemble other illnesses, so early and accurate diagnosis matters. This dedicated clinic brings several specialties together to evaluate pituitary diseases and tumours and to plan diagnosis and treatment using modern imaging, laboratory and treatment methods. MedLuxLife coordinates your referral, records and appointments at our partner hospital.
cards: Early diagnosis
Focused assessment of symptoms, hormone levels and imaging to identify pituitary conditions as early as possible.
Pituitary tumour care
Evaluation and treatment planning for pituitary tumours and other diseases of the gland.
Multidisciplinary team

Care involves endocrinologists specialised in pituitary disease, neurosurgeons, neuroradiologists, neuropathologists, neuro-ophthalmologists, radiation oncologists, anaesthesiologists and supporting health staff.
Weekly case conferences
Pituitary cases are discussed at regular multidisciplinary meetings, which external physicians can also attend with their own cases.
Education programmes
The clinic runs educational programmes on pituitary disease for patients and physicians.
International collaboration
The clinic works together with international organisations in the field of pituitary disease.
docs_extra: Previous pituitary MRI scans on CD/DVD with reports
Recent hormone test results
Visual field test results, if available

psychiatry.title: Psychiatry
psychiatry.lead: Psychiatry is concerned with the evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of mental health problems, looking at emotional, cognitive and behavioural symptoms as a whole. The department offers support for difficulties ranging from stress and life challenges to more serious mental health conditions, with treatment plans tailored to each person. MedLuxLife can arrange confidential consultations at our partner hospital, including interpreter support where needed.
cards: Psychiatric evaluation and diagnosis
A comprehensive assessment that considers medical history, symptoms and living circumstances to understand underlying causes.
Medication treatment
Medication may be prescribed where appropriate, with regular follow-up to monitor its effect and safety.
Psychotherapy
Talking therapies including cognitive behavioural therapy, psychoanalysis, family therapy and group therapy.
Crisis intervention
Prompt support in psychiatric emergencies such as suicidal thoughts, acute anxiety attacks or psychotic symptoms.
Rehabilitation and support
Programmes for people with long-term mental health conditions, focusing on daily living skills, work and social integration.
docs_extra: List of current and previous psychiatric medications
Previous psychiatric or psychological reports

psychology.title: Psychology
psychology.lead: Health includes emotional, cognitive and mental wellbeing as well as physical health. The clinical psychology unit offers psychological assessment and support for children, adolescents and adults, including school-related assessments, structured education programmes and therapy for patients undergoing cancer treatment. MedLuxLife can arrange appointments at our partner hospital and help with language and scheduling.
cards: Support for children
Help with a wide range of emotional, behavioural and developmental difficulties, using cognitive behavioural therapy and play therapy.
School problems
Assessment of attention, learning and reading difficulties, followed by individual training plans based on the results.
Psychological testing
Developmental screening tests, intelligence tests, learning difficulty tests and attention tests.
Education programmes
Individual attention-enhancing programmes and reading disorder (dyslexia) programmes for children.
Support for adolescents
Cognitive behavioural approaches for behaviour problems, family conflict, mood difficulties and exam anxiety.
Support for adults
Cognitive behavioural therapy for depression, anxiety, OCD, panic, trauma, and family, relationship or work-related problems.
Psycho-oncology
Patients treated in the oncology unit are invited to psychotherapy, including cognitive behavioural therapy and meaning-centred therapy for cancer and grief, to help them adapt and cope.
Seminars for schools
Seminars for parents and children can be organised at the request of schools.
list: Children: toilet problems (toilet training, stool withholding, soiling)
Children: family difficulties such as divorce or bereavement (post-traumatic stress)
Children: physical complaints such as abdominal pain or nausea
Adults: bereavement, accidents or divorce (post-traumatic stress)
docs_extra: School reports or teacher feedback (for children)
Previous psychological test results

radiology.title: Radiology
radiology.lead: The radiology department provides a broad range of diagnostic imaging, from MRI and CT to PET-CT, mammography and ultrasound, together with interventional radiology. Images are acquired digitally and stored with their reports in a central archive, making them available to treating teams across the hospital. MedLuxLife can schedule imaging at our partner hospital as part of a check-up or treatment plan and arrange for your images and reports to be shared with you.
cards: MRI
3 Tesla magnetic resonance imaging for detailed views of soft tissues, the brain, spine and joints.
CT
64-slice multi-slice computed tomography for fast cross-sectional imaging.
PET-CT
Combined functional and anatomical imaging, often used in cancer assessment.
Digital X-ray and portable X-ray
Conventional digital radiography, with portable units available for patients who cannot be moved.
Ultrasound
Ultrasonography including Doppler, 3D and 4D imaging.
Digital mammography
Breast imaging for screening and diagnosis.
Fluoroscopy and C-arm
Real-time X-ray imaging used for dynamic studies and to guide procedures.
Digital angiography
Imaging of blood vessels for diagnosis and to guide treatment.
Bone densitometry
Measurement of bone density to assess osteoporosis.
Interventional radiology
Many vascular diseases can be diagnosed and treated with image-guided, minimally invasive techniques, avoiding open surgery in suitable cases.
Digital archive (PACS and RIS)
Images and reports are stored centrally and shared securely with clinical teams, and can be exchanged with external centres.
Research laboratory
The department includes a research laboratory supporting work in medical imaging.
docs_extra: Previous imaging on CD/DVD with reports, for comparison

rheumatology.title: Rheumatology
rheumatology.lead: Rheumatology is a subspecialty dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of rheumatic diseases, which are common, often long-lasting and can lead to pain, loss of function and reduced quality of life if not managed appropriately. Because these conditions can affect many organs, care is coordinated with several other specialties. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and follow-up at our partner hospital and keeps your records organised between visits.
cards: Diagnosis of rheumatic diseases
Specialist evaluation of joint pain, stiffness, inflammation and related symptoms to establish an accurate diagnosis.
Treatment and long-term management
Individual treatment plans aimed at controlling symptoms, preserving function and supporting quality of life.
Interdisciplinary follow-up
Joint care with dermatology, neurology, orthopaedics and traumatology, physical therapy and rehabilitation, and ophthalmology when several organs are involved.
Fibromyalgia team care
Treatment for widespread pain and fatigue planned jointly by rheumatologists, physical therapy and rehabilitation specialists, psychiatrists and neurologists.
docs_extra: Previous blood tests, including inflammatory markers and antibody results
List of current medications, including biologic therapies

thoracic-surgery.title: Thoracic Surgery
thoracic-surgery.lead: Thoracic surgery treats diseases of the organs and tissues within the chest, excluding the heart, including the lungs, airways, chest wall, pleura, diaphragm, mediastinum and oesophagus. The department uses fibreoptic and endoscopic equipment, minimally invasive surgical tools and imaging from virtual bronchoscopy to PET-CT, supported by pathology and laboratory services. MedLuxLife coordinates evaluation and surgery at our partner hospital, from sharing your scans to planning your recovery stay.
cards: Lung cancer surgery
Surgical treatment of lung cancer by open surgery or, in suitable cases, fully endoscopic techniques.
Lungs and main airways
Surgical and endoscopic procedures for diseases of the lungs and the major airways.
Airway stents and endoscopic airway opening
For patients who cannot undergo surgery, stents and endoscopic procedures may help relieve breathing symptoms.
Thoracic outlet syndrome
Surgical treatment for compression of nerves and blood vessels that can cause arm pain, coldness, numbness and weakness.
Chest wall diseases
Treatment of congenital and acquired conditions of the chest wall.
Pleura, diaphragm and chest cavity
Care for diseases of the lung lining, the diaphragm and the chest cavity.
Mediastinal surgery
Surgical procedures in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the chest.
Oesophageal surgery
Treatment of oesophageal motility disorders, benign and malignant tumours, hernias and reflux-related disease.
Advanced diagnostics
Imaging such as virtual bronchoscopy and PET-CT, together with pathology and laboratory support, to guide treatment decisions.
docs_extra: Recent chest CT or PET-CT on CD/DVD with reports
Lung function test results

thyroid-parathyroid-diseases-and-surgery.title: Thyroid and Parathyroid Diseases and Surgery Clinic
thyroid-parathyroid-diseases-and-surgery.lead: This multidisciplinary clinic is dedicated exclusively to diseases of the thyroid and parathyroid glands, offering early diagnosis together with medical and surgical treatment. Specialists from seven fields evaluate each case jointly, following current scientific evidence. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment, tests and any surgery at our partner hospital, with clear communication at every stage.
cards: Multidisciplinary team
Specialists in endocrine surgery, endocrinology, nuclear medicine, radiology, pathology, genetics and bioengineering work together on each case.
Thyroid and parathyroid ultrasound
Dedicated ultrasound examination of the thyroid and parathyroid glands.
Scintigraphy
Thyroid (Tc99m), parathyroid (MIBI) and DOTATATE scintigraphy to assess gland function and locate abnormal tissue.
Choline PET
PET imaging that can help locate parathyroid tissue when other tests are inconclusive.
Function tests
Laboratory testing of thyroid and parathyroid hormone function.
Biopsy
Fine needle and Tru-Cut biopsy to examine nodules and suspicious tissue.
Radioactive iodine therapy
Radioactive iodine treatment for suitable thyroid conditions.
Lithium-supported radioactive iodine therapy
In selected cases, lithium may be used alongside radioactive iodine to support the treatment.
Radiofrequency ablation
Non-surgical treatment of thyroid nodules using radiofrequency energy.
Thyroid and parathyroid surgery
Operations using classical and microsurgical techniques, as well as the scarless transoral approach (TOETVA).
Parathyroid transplantation
Reimplantation of parathyroid tissue to help preserve gland function where needed.
list: Surgery with classical and microsurgical techniques
docs_extra: Previous thyroid ultrasound and scintigraphy reports
Recent thyroid and parathyroid hormone and calcium results

transfusion-center.title: Transfusion Centre
transfusion-center.lead: The transfusion centre supports inpatients and other patients who need blood component therapy, cellular therapy, therapeutic apheresis or specialised laboratory diagnostics. Blood components and cellular therapy products are collected and prepared on site, and the centre also supports clinical research and training in transfusion medicine. MedLuxLife coordinates these services at our partner hospital as part of your wider treatment plan.
cards: Blood component therapy
Safe and appropriate administration of blood products for patients who need them during treatment.
Cellular therapy
Collection and preparation of cellular therapy products used in patient care.
Therapeutic apheresis
Procedures that separate and remove or replace specific blood components as part of treatment.
Specialised laboratory diagnostics
Diagnostic and compatibility testing to support safe transfusion.
Blood bank
Provides packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma and platelets.
Research and training
Support for clinical research and advanced training in transfusion medicine and related technologies.
docs_extra: Blood group card or previous blood group test
Records of previous transfusions or transfusion reactions

urology.title: Urology
urology.lead: Urology covers the diagnosis and treatment of conditions of the urinary tract in women and men and of the male reproductive organs, from urological cancers and prostate disease to kidney stones, infertility and incontinence. Care is personalised and coordinated with internal medicine, oncology, gynaecology and psychiatry when needed. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and treatment at our partner hospital and supports you before, during and after your stay.
cards: Urological oncology
Diagnosis and treatment of prostate, bladder, kidney and testicular cancer.
Benign prostatic hyperplasia
Treatment options for an enlarged prostate, including laser prostate surgery (GreenLight).
Focal therapy for prostate cancer
HIFU focal therapy may be an option for suitable patients with prostate cancer.
Stone disease
Treatment of kidney stones with flexible endoscopic methods and treatment of urinary tract stones.
Andrology
Assessment and treatment of male infertility and erectile problems.
Female urology
Diagnosis and treatment of urinary incontinence, female sexual dysfunction and conditions of the urinary tract and pelvic organs.
Multidisciplinary care
Collaboration with internal medicine, oncology, obstetrics and gynaecology, and psychiatry where appropriate.
list: Conditions of the female urinary tract and pelvic organs
docs_extra: Recent PSA results (for men)
Previous urinary tract imaging reports
